newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT--Bruised dollar fights to stem losses.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT--Bruised dollar fights to stem losses.

text.p: After several days of knocking on the door of significant technical resistance levels, the dollar was forced to grope for support Wednesday and remains vulnerable, chartists said.
The greenback punched through supports at 1.5110 and 1.5070 marks after a surprising widening of the U.S. trade gap in July and sank to the 1.5040 area before recovering.

The failure of the dollar to extend a recent rally past crucial resistance at 1.5165 marks could signal the start of a prolonged, if choppy ride back down as much as four pfennigs, technical analysts said.

"That (1.5165 marks) resistance area was very important. it was a 0.618 (percent) Fibonnaci retracement of the decline from the May high at 1.5488. It's a logical place for the dollar to turn back down," said Dan Ascani, president of Global Market Strategists Inc.
Key support for the dollar now rests at 1.4950 and 1.49 marks, and a failure to hold there could bring big losses, Ascani said.
"If we get confirmation that this is not just a pullback in a bullish market, but an actual correction, the dollar should drop toward the 1.4650 marks area," he added.
A report Wednesday showed the U.S. trade gap ballooned 42.6 percent to $11.7 bilion in July from June, quickly sending the dollar lower.
Dollar-buyers had enjoyed steady shrinkage in the trade gap in recent months and the sudden reversal caused a massive retreat of current support levels, technical analysts said.
"The trade number largely affects the yen," Ascani said. "We're seeing the trend change in dollar/yen. All of our oscillators are turning down."
Initial Fibonacci support comes in just below 109 yen, roughly where Wednesday's slump ended, analysts said. Further down, chart congestion should prop up the dollar at 108.50 and 108 yen.
Mark/yen continues to vacillate in a narrow range, but the current chart patterns suggest the next move will be a test of support, analysts said.
Current resistance sits at 72.50, with support looking vulnerable at 72 and more reliable at 71.50, analysts said.
